+# Contributing to this project
+
+Thank you for your interest in contributing! This document will guide you through the development setup, testing, and pull request process.
+
+## Project Overview
+
+This project provides utility modules for inventory reconciliation, pricing cache management, and shipment planning. The codebase is written in Python and focuses on simplicity and correctness.
+
+## Development Setup
+
+### Prerequisites
+
+- Python 3.8 or higher
+- Git
+
+### Setting up your environment
+
+1. **Clone the repository:**
+   ```bash
+   git clone <repository-url>
+   cd <repository-directory>
+   ```
+
+2. **Create a virtual environment:**
+   ```bash
+   python -m venv venv
+   source venv/bin/activate  # On Windows: venv\Scripts\activate
+   ```
+
+3. **Install development dependencies:**
+   ```bash
+   pip install -e .  # Install the project in editable mode if setup.py exists
+   ```
+
+   If there's no setup.py, you can run your code directly or install any dependencies:
+   ```bash
+   pip install pytest  # For running tests
+   ```
+
+## Running Tests
+
+Tests can be run using pytest:
+
+```bash
+pytest
+```
+
+For verbose output:
+```bash
+pytest -v
+```
+
+To run specific test files:
+```bash
+pytest tests/test_inventory_reconciliation.py
+```
+
+## Before Opening a Pull Request
+
+### 1. Code Quality
+
+- Follow PEP 8 style guidelines
+- Keep functions focused and simple
+- Add docstrings to public functions explaining what they do
+- Avoid unnecessary comments; code should be self-explanatory
+
+### 2. Testing
+
+- Write tests for any new functionality
+- Ensure all existing tests still pass
+- Aim for reasonable test coverage of critical paths
+
+### 3. Commit Messages
+
+- Write clear, descriptive commit messages
+- Use the present tense ("add feature" not "added feature")
+- Keep the first line under 50 characters
+- Provide additional context in the commit body if needed
+
+Example:
+```
+Fix inventory reconciliation for edge case with null quantities
+
+Previously, reconcile() would include rows with null quantities in
+results. Now they're properly filtered out before returning.
+```
+
+### 4. Pull Request Checklist
+
+Before submitting your PR, ensure:
+
+- [ ] All tests pass (`pytest`)
+- [ ] Your code follows PEP 8 style guidelines
+- [ ] You've added tests for new functionality
+- [ ] Your commit messages are clear and descriptive
+- [ ] You've updated documentation if needed (especially docstrings)
+- [ ] You've checked for any obvious bugs or edge cases
+
+### 5. Pull Request Guidelines
+
+- Create a clear, concise PR title
+- In the description, explain what changes you made and why
+- Reference any related issues
+- Keep PRs focused on a single concern when possible
+
+## Questions?
+
+If you have questions about the project or development process, please open an issue or reach out to the maintainers.
+
+Happy contributing!
